author: reek
body: A flow-field swarm, as a [Device] compute kernel. One GPU thread owns one particle. Each thread reads its particle's state (px, py, vx, vy) from an input buffer, steers its velocity toward a procedural flow field derived from position and time (fixed-point trig), integrates with inertia so the paths curve smoothly, wraps around the screen, and writes the new state to an output buffer. The host ping-pongs the two buffers each frame.

author: reek
body: This is emitter-tractable today: pure helpers plus one act-block kernel with buffer loads and stores, no per-neighbour loop. True neighbour-based boids (separation/alignment/cohesion) needs a bounded loop over the state buffer, which is recursion in Codex and requires recursion-to-loop lowering plus storage-pointer helper parameters in the WGSL plug -- the next emitter milestone.

author: reek
body: The flow angle at a point cycles across space and drifts with time, giving a few large vortices that evolve. cos/sin of the angle give the target velocity direction; sw-speed scales the magnitude.

author: reek
body: Inertia: ease the velocity toward the flow so paths curve instead of snapping. Positions wrap toroidally.
